title: The posturographic sensory hierarchy, certified: COP sway rises monotonically Open-Firm < Closed-Firm < Open-Foam < Closed-Foam (Friedman Q bit-for-bit vs base R, machine-precision vs scipy)

dataset.name: BDS -- a public data set of human balance evaluations (Santos & Duarte 2016)
dataset.record: force-plate COP (COPx/COPy) at 100 Hz, 60 s quiet standing; 2x2 vision (open/closed) x surface (firm/foam) design; 158 subjects with all four conditions
dataset.citation: Santos DA, Duarte M. A public data set of human balance evaluations. PeerJ 2016;4:e2648. doi:10.7717/peerj.2648.

proposition: Standing balance integrates vision and proprioception; the BDS challenges both in a 2x2 (eyes open/closed x firm/foam) design measured on every subject. Because the four conditions are repeated measures, the correct omnibus is the non-parametric Friedman test. Each subject's mean COP path length per condition comes from the certified swayMetrics; the NEWLY-AUTHORED friedmanTest compares the four conditions across 158 subjects, reproducing base R stats::friedman.test BIT-FOR-BIT and scipy.stats.friedmanchisquare to machine precision. The conditions differ overwhelmingly (Q=420.1, df=3, p~9.7e-91) with a MONOTONE mean-rank order Open-Firm (1.31) < Closed-Firm (1.69) < Open-Foam (3.08) < Closed-Foam (3.92): each sensory challenge adds sway, and softening the surface (proprioception) dominates closing the eyes (vision).

claims.statement: tie-corrected Friedman chi-square of COP path length across the four vision x surface conditions
mean rank of the Open-Firm condition (best balance, lowest rank)
mean rank of the Closed-Foam condition (worst balance, highest rank)
mean ranks increase monotonically Open-Firm < Closed-Firm < Open-Foam < Closed-Foam
subjects with all four conditions (complete blocks)

validation.reference: The newly-authored friedmanTest op (tie-corrected non-parametric repeated-measures omnibus) is validated against BOTH scipy.stats.friedmanchisquare AND base R stats::friedman.test on the identical 158 x 4 complete-block matrix -- a double reference. All three compute the tie-corrected Friedman chi-square of COP path length across the four conditions; base R friedman.test agrees BIT-FOR-BIT (|diff| = 0) and scipy agrees to machine precision (|diff| ~ 6e-14, floating-point associativity in the rank-total accumulation). The per-subject per-condition COP path lengths come from PhysioMoCap::swayMetrics (path_length, certified against Prieto in the sibling sway-posturography-bds case). The per-condition mean ranks are reported.
validation.data: REAL -- Santos & Duarte (2016) BDS, force-plate COP at 100 Hz; 158 subjects x 4 vision x surface quiet-standing conditions (complete blocks)
validation.note: The reproducible findings are (1) friedmanTest reproduces base R friedman.test bit-for-bit and scipy.stats.friedmanchisquare to machine precision on the 4-condition balance design; (2) COP sway rises monotonically across the four sensory conditions. HONEST scope: (1) this AUTHORS A NEW OP, friedmanTest (the within-subject, distribution-free counterpart of the certified oneWayAnova), and reuses the certified swayMetrics op (path_length, validated against Prieto in the sibling sway-posturography-bds case) for the per-condition COP path length; (2) the tie-corrected Friedman chi-square reproduces base R stats::friedman.test BIT-FOR-BIT (|diff| = 0) and scipy.stats.friedmanchisquare to MACHINE PRECISION (|diff| ~ 6e-14 -- floating-point associativity in the rank-total accumulation), so base R is the exact reference and scipy the machine-precision cross-check; (3) the four conditions are REPEATED MEASURES (every subject measured under all four), so the Friedman test is the correct omnibus (a between-subjects ANOVA/Kruskal-Wallis would ignore the within-subject pairing); (4) the finding: the four conditions differ overwhelmingly -- Q = 420.1 on 3 df, p ~ 9.7e-91 -- with a MONOTONE mean-rank order Open-Firm (1.31) < Closed-Firm (1.69) < Open-Foam (3.08) < Closed-Foam (3.92); each sensory challenge adds sway, and softening the surface (degrading proprioception; the firm->foam rank jump ~1.4) dominates closing the eyes (removing vision; the open->closed jump ~0.4), so on foam vision matters most while on firm ground healthy adults barely need it; the condition-mean path lengths are 59.6 / 65.7 / 177.3 / 222.4 cm; (5) this closes the Romberg case's open question about how the sensory contributions combine, tested correctly for the repeated-measures design; the omnibus certifies the conditions differ -- post-hoc pairwise (e.g. Nemenyi) would order every pair; (6) a real cohort (ASSOCIATION, NOT CAUSATION), one per-subject mean per condition; run_simulation = FALSE (deterministic).

open_questions.q: The omnibus certifies that the four conditions differ, with a monotone mean-rank order; post-hoc pairwise tests (e.g. Nemenyi/Conover) would establish which specific pairs differ and quantify the vision vs proprioception contributions separately. A two-way analysis (vision x surface with an interaction term) would test whether vision matters more on foam than on firm ground (the pattern the ranks suggest). The Friedman omnibus shown here is the correct first-line repeated-measures test. Documented, not escalated.
